title: wiqd Extension Manifest

$schema.description: JSON Schema pointer for editor validation/completion.

workflows.description: Contributed-workflows directory, relative to the extension package root.

references.description: Contributed-references directory, relative to the extension package root.

skills.description: Contributed-skills directory, relative to the extension package root.

runtime.description: Trusted in-process runtime backend. Mutually exclusive with `upstream`: an extension picks at most one command/auth execution backend. Its mere presence does not import code — a command or auth action must declare `handler` to actually invoke the factory-created adapter.

activationWhen.description: Conditional participation gate. A single `<flag> == <value>` equality that gates the WHOLE extension on a feature-flag value, so one flag can select exactly one member of a mutually-exclusive set (e.g. `plugin-core-engine` choosing the atk subprocess backend vs. the fxcore in-process backend). The host branches only on the flag name/value, never on extension identity. Absent means the extension always participates.

eulaGate.description: EULA gate: how the host recognizes this tool's "EULA required" handshake, what to surface, and how `wiqd eula accept` accepts. Declared once per extension; the host applies it to every command the extension contributes.

flags.description: Feature flags this extension declares; merged into the host flag registry.

configKeys.description: Persisted `wiqd config set` keys this extension declares: the host merges these into its known-key set generically — it never hardcodes a domain key name — so `wiqd config set <key>=<value>` can validate/store/ clear an extension's own settings with zero host change.

description: A wiqd extension manifest (`wiqd-extension.json`). Declares the commands, upstream tool, auth providers, doctor checks, and mock responses an extension contributes to the wiqd host.

provider.description: Built-in primitive name. Unknown names yield no completions (fail closed).

CompletionSpec.description: Declarative completion source for an option value. Names a host-provided completion PRIMITIVE (a sync, local, fail-closed candidate generator that runs per keystroke inside the `__complete` process). Static value lists do NOT belong here — use `choices`/`enum`, which already become the option's commander choices and take precedence.

name.description: Default row label (e.g. "workiq --json"). Individual outcomes MAY override it.

description.description: Documents the check's intent. Not rendered in the row.

binary.description: Binary resolved (via `pathEnvVar` → npm `.bin` walk → PATH) and probed.

pathEnvVar.description: Environment variable consulted first when resolving `binary` (e.g. WORKIQ_PATH).

timeoutSeconds.description: Probe timeout in seconds. Defaults to 10.

missing.description: Outcome when `binary` cannot be resolved. Defaults to warn "<binary> not found".

onError.description: Outcome when the probe throws (spawn failure / timeout). Defaults to warn "Could not probe <binary>".

rules.description: Ordered result rules; the first whose `when` matches the completed probe wins.

DoctorCheck.description: A manifest-declared health check run by `wiqd doctor`. The host resolves `binary`, probes it with `args`, and maps the result to a row via the declarative outcomes — it never branches on the extension's identity. The shape is rich enough to express a tri-state probe (the workiq `--json` check): `missing` (binary absent), `onError` (probe threw), and an ordered `rules` list (first match wins) over the completed probe.

name.description: Row-label override for this outcome (e.g. the `missing` outcome labels the row "workiq").

message.description: Row message. Supports `${exitCode}` interpolation against the probe result.

when.description: Match condition. Every present field must match; an omitted `when` is a catch-all.

flag.description: Canonical long flag, e.g. `--environment`. MUST be a long flag: a short-style `-e` renders as `---e` once combined with the alias list, and commander rejects it.

aliases.description: At most ONE additional long flag. Commander accepts a maximum of two long flags per option and the canonical `flag` occupies the second slot, so a longer list is rejected at build time. An alias that collides with a flag the command already declares is dropped; the canonical `flag` is still registered.

env.description: Env var the per-invocation value is injected into on the child process. MUST match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`; process-influencing names (`NODE_OPTIONS`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `PATH`, ...) are refused at runtime.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code surfaced as `error.code` in the `--json` envelope. Lives in the manifest so failure classes stay a domain concern — the host only plumbs whatever the extension declares.

args.description: Args appended to the extension's resolved upstream binary to accept the EULA (e.g. `["accept-eula"]`). This is the ONLY source of the args wiqd runs — never derived from parsed output. wiqd runs this tuple solely via the interactive `wiqd eula accept` handler.

displayCommand.description: Raw upstream command shown as the fallback CTA (e.g. `workiq accept-eula`).

EulaDetectCondition.description: Recognition conditions for the EULA handshake. Extends the doctor `when` vocabulary (`exitCode`/`exitCodeNot`/`stdoutContains`/`stdoutMatches`) with `stderrMatches` and the structured `stdoutJson { path, equals }` discriminator. All present conditions must match (logical AND). There is no `exitCode` constraint by default, so a EULA payload emitted with exit 0 still matches.

EulaExtract.description: Display-only capture rules. MUST NOT influence `accept.args`.

group.description: 1-based capture group index for `stdoutMatches`. Defaults to 1.

EulaExtractRule.description: A single display-value capture rule. Either a stdout regex with a capture `group`, or a `stdoutJson` path read from the parsed stdout JSON.

tool.description: Display name of the tool whose EULA is unaccepted, and the `<tool>` selector for `wiqd eula accept <tool>` / `wiqd eula status`. Shown to the user; never used for host branching.

eulaUrl.description: Static EULA URL to display; overridden by a matching `extract.eulaUrl`.

detect.description: Recognition conditions evaluated against the completed upstream result.

extract.description: Optional display-only capture rules pulled from the tool's own output.

EulaGate.description: Manifest-contributed EULA gate. Lets a downstream tool declare — with zero host change — how wiqd recognizes its "you must accept the EULA" handshake, what tool name / URL to surface, and how `wiqd eula accept` performs the (interactive, human-confirmed) acceptance.

path.description: Dot/bracket path into the parsed stdout JSON (e.g. `isError`, `error.code`, `items[0].id`).

equals.description: Value the resolved path must strictly equal.

EulaStdoutJsonPredicate.description: Structured JSON-path discriminator over the tool's stdout JSON.

positional.description: When true, this arg is registered as a commander POSITIONAL argument (`wiqd agent review gate <name>`) instead of a `--flag`. The builder uses commander's optional `[name]` form and leaves `required: true` enforcement to ManifestExecutor, so parent command args never block child subcommand dispatch and `defaultFrom` can populate values before the final required check. The parsed value threads into the executor's expression/argMap context under the bare arg `name` (no leading `--`), so a positional and a flag are interchangeable from the manifest's `argMap`/`bindArgs` point of view. Defaults to `false` (flag behavior).

discover.description: Command that finds this option's value, shown when the option is missing. "You're missing --id" is half an error; the other half is where to get one. Declared per option because only the extension knows which lookup applies.

gatedBy.description: Optional feature-flag gate for a SINGLE option/positional. When set, the host skips registering this arg unless the named boolean flag is enabled — so the flag hides the arg from `--help` AND makes it inert (an unregistered option can never be parsed, so any `argMap`/`devuiProxy` expression keyed on it evaluates falsy). Fail-closed: an unknown or disabled flag hides the arg. Use this to gate a capability-specific flag on an otherwise-always-available command (e.g. `--devui` on `agent ask`, gated by the `devui` flag).

complete.description: Optional shell-completion source for this option's VALUE. Lets an extension own the completion of its own args (e.g. ATK declaring that `--env` completes from `env/.env.<name>`) instead of the host hardcoding that domain knowledge. The host runs the named primitive in-process during `wiqd __complete` — see completion/completion-primitives.ts.

handler.description: Trusted in-process invocation for a runtime-backed auth action. Present instead of subprocess-only fields (`args`, `signedInPattern`, etc.) when the extension is runtime-backed; the action resolves through the same cached adapter as ordinary handler commands (in-process-manifest-handler.md §12). An auth command MUST NOT mix subprocess and handler shapes.

interactive.description: Marks the action as inherently interactive (e.g. a browser sign-in) so the host grants it an extended subprocess timeout.

interactiveArgs.description: Extra args appended to `args` for `login` when the user passes `wiqd auth login --interactive` (e.g. ATK `-i true`).

nonInteractiveArgs.description: Extra args appended to `args` for `login` when `--interactive` is NOT set (e.g. ATK `-i false`). Lets the host force a non-interactive default while still forcing a real sign-in.

signedInPattern.description: Regex (optionally with an `account` named group) applied to the `status` action's combined output. A match means signed in. Required for upstream tools whose status command exits 0 in both signed-in and signed-out states (e.g. ATK's `auth list`), where the exit code is not a reliable signal. Also used by `login` to verify an identity was actually acquired after the login subprocess exits 0.

providerId.description: Stable provider identifier surfaced by `wiqd auth status`.

displayName.description: Human-readable provider name shown in auth output.

signInLabel.description: User-facing service name for the mid-flow "Signing in to <X>..." progress line (e.g. "Microsoft 365"). Falls back to `displayName` when absent. Lets an extension present a friendly product name in sign-in UX without leaking an internal tool name, while the host stays domain-agnostic.

binary.description: Upstream binary that performs the auth flow (defaults to `upstream.binary`).

applicability.description: Which command surfaces this provider applies to (e.g. "all").

gatedBy.description: Optional command-availability feature-flag gate for an individual command (e.g. the opt-in `monitor` command). When set, the host skips registering this command unless the named boolean flag is enabled. Fail-closed semantics live in `feature-flags/gating.ts`.

namespaceOverride.description: When a command is mounted under an `additionalNamespaces` group (e.g. `feedback` rather than the manifest's primary `agent` namespace), this carries the mounted namespace so telemetry and host-level error envelopes report `feedback.submit` instead of the misleading `agent.submit`.

ExtensionConfigKey.description: A persisted config key declared by an extension's manifest. Mirrors the host's own hardcoded `VALID_KEYS` shape (commands/config-set.ts) so `wiqd config set`/`config` treat a contributed key exactly like a built-in one: validated against `enumValues` when present, clearable via `key=` when `clearable` is true, and echoed un-redacted (contributed keys are assumed non-secret; an extension needing secret handling should not use this generic mechanism).

ExtensionFlagDefinition.description: A feature flag declared by an extension's manifest. Mirrors the host `FlagDefinition` (feature-flags/types.ts); the registry merges these into the host flag set and validates the merged whole. Kept self-contained here so the manifest schema generator resolves it without importing the feature-flags module.

wiqd.description: Semver range for the wiqd host; the host refuses to load if its version is out of range.

node.description: Documented minimum Node.js version. Not enforced by wiqd.

path.description: Directory path relative to the extension package root.

target.description: Dot-separated own-property path from the factory result (e.g. `engine`, `auth.session`).

method.description: Callable own-property name on the resolved target.

args.description: Ordered method arguments; nested strings support recursive `${...}` resolution. Defaults to [].

HandlerConfig.description: Trusted in-process invocation target (manifest-schema.md §5.2). Replaces the subprocess spawn stage with a method call on the extension's `runtime` adapter. `target`/`method` are resolved by safe own-property walking (no eval); the host appends the effective AbortSignal after the resolved `args`.

aliases.description: Additional names under which this command is registered in the CLI. Commander wires each alias via `.alias()` so help text, completion, and routing all resolve the alternative names to the same handler. Distinct from `alias` on `ExtensionArg`, which is for option short-flags.

preTransformPostActions.description: Post-preTransform upstream mutations gated on what preTransform observed (e.g. enabling an experimental upstream flag). Each entry is a `{ when?, upstreamCall }` action.

container.description: Marks this as a pure command GROUP (e.g. `agent add`) that exists only to carry a `--help` description for its subcommands. The builder sets the description but attaches NO action handler, so invoking the bare group shows help instead of dispatching an (empty) upstream call. A container MUST NOT declare `options` or `argMap`: the host skips registering them (they would be inert since no action ever runs), and `validateManifest()` flags a container that declares either as an `invalid-container` finding.

skipUpstreamWhen.description: Skip the upstream spawn step when this expression is truthy.

requiresAuth.description: Run the extension's subprocess auth status probe before spawning. A definitive signed-out verdict returns exit 2; unavailable or inconclusive probes fail open. Subprocess-backed commands only.

devuiProxy.description: Optionally route the upstream call through the local Work IQ DevUI proxy when `when` is truthy and DevUI is reachable, so the call is captured + inspectable there. The DevUI response (the upstream's own `--json` shape) replaces the upstream output, so the command's transform/render are unchanged. ANY failure (DevUI unreachable, non-2xx) silently falls back to spawning the binary.

exitIf.description: Convert a passing spawn into a failure when `condition` is truthy.

omitRawResponse.description: When true, `buildJsonData` does NOT auto-inject `data.response = upstream.stdout.trim()`. Use this when the command runs a post-upstream transform that already exposes structured fields (e.g. `responseText`, `conversationId`) and the raw upstream stdout would be redundant or leak ANSI/prose. Verbose mode still surfaces the raw stdout on stderr.

jsonOmitPath.description: When true, `buildJsonData` does NOT auto-inject `data.path` (the resolved output/cwd path). Use this for API-backed commands whose JSON envelope is a fixed, documented field set (e.g. `account.enroll`) where an absolute filesystem path is meaningless and leaks the caller's cwd into scripted output.

jsonOmitComputed.description: Computed keys to withhold from the `--json` envelope. Computed values are spread wholesale into `data`, so an intermediate declared only to feed a later expression would otherwise become part of the published contract.

handler.description: Trusted in-process invocation. Replaces the upstream spawn stage with a method call on the extension's `runtime` adapter. Mutually exclusive with the subprocess-control fields (argMap, noUpstream, skipUpstreamWhen, stdioPassthrough, devuiProxy, preTransform, preTransformPostActions, transform, errors, exitCode, omitRawResponse, nativeDryRunHandler, requiresAuth); `delegateWhen` is the one permitted alongside it.

nativeDryRunHandler.description: When set, and the user passes `--dry-run`, the executor delegates to this named native TypeScript handler instead of spawning the upstream binary. The name must be registered in the host's dry-run handler registry. This lets an ATK-backed command (e.g. `agent publish`) expose a no-submit validation path without any host code knowing which command it is — the manifest owns the routing decision.

gatedBy.description: Optional command-availability feature-flag gate for the manifest-driven command definition (e.g. the opt-in `monitor` command). When set, the host skips registering this command unless the named boolean flag is enabled.

when.description: Optional guard expression evaluated against the command scope. Only meaningful inside a variant list — the first variant whose `when` is truthy (or absent) wins.

stdoutFile.description: Path (relative to the extension's manifest directory) to a file whose contents supply the upstream stdout. Mutually exclusive with `stdout` — lets large, realistic payloads live in readable `mocks/*.json` fixtures instead of escaped one-line strings. The file content is `${...}` interpolated against the command scope, same as inline `stdout`.

stderrFile.description: File-backed counterpart to `stderr`. Mutually exclusive with `stderr`.

ManifestMockResponseEntry.description: A response entry is either a single response or an ordered list of variants. When it is a list, the first variant whose `when` expression is truthy (or that has no `when`) is selected. This lets a command declare a conditional error path (e.g. an error variant gated on a sentinel input) ahead of its unconditional success variant — without making the success path always fail.

copyFrom.description: Copy an existing file's bytes into `path` — the faithful analogue of a local copy-from-source op (e.g. `agent env add` copying `env/.env.<from>`). The value is `${...}` interpolated. The resolved source MUST live within the destination file's directory subtree, so a manifest can never read arbitrary host files. Mutually exclusive with `content`/`contentBase64`/`clear`.

clear.description: Truncate the existing file at `path` to empty — the faithful analogue of `agent env reset`. Uses `truncateSync`, so it fails if the target is absent; the command's preflight is the user-facing guard. Mutually exclusive with `content`/`contentBase64`/`copyFrom`.

ManifestNamespace.description: A command group mounted under a non-primary namespace (e.g. `feedback`). Every key is a command definition, except two reserved meta keys: - `_description` — string help text for the namespace command. - `_gatedBy` — a boolean feature-flag name; when its gate is closed the host hides the ENTIRE namespace this extension contributes (the container is never created and no child is registered). Fail-closed, mirroring the per-command and per-option gates.

module.description: Relative ESM JavaScript path; absolute/URL/bare/built-in/escaping paths are invalid.

factory.description: Own, callable named export matching /^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$/ returning the adapter.

capabilities.description: Host capabilities handed to the factory. Only `logger` in v1; defaults to [].

RuntimeConfig.description: Trusted in-process runtime declaration (manifest-schema.md §3.5). The host imports `module` (a relative ESM path contained by the extension root), resolves `factory` as an own callable named export, calls it once per process, and passes only the requested `capabilities`. Execution, trust, caching, and disposal live in in-process-manifest-handler.md.

installCommand.description: The exact, argv-splittable shell command (no quoted args) that installs this upstream binary — distinct from `installHint`, which is a human sentence that MAY wrap the command in prose. The prerequisite preflight gate's consent-gated install offer runs this command verbatim, so it must be runnable as-is. Bundled tools (ATK, eval, workiq) set this to the wiqd installer command rather than a direct sub-package install: all three are transitive dependencies of the wiqd package, so reinstalling wiqd is what actually restores them at the tested/pinned version. It is also exactly what `wiqd update` runs, and matches the pre-existing `wiqd doctor` remediation convention, so this offer can never disagree with doctor's guidance. Omit when the tool has no single runnable install command at all; the gate then falls back to printing `installHint` without offering to run anything.

timeoutHint.description: Extension-owned recovery sentence appended when the host kills this upstream for exceeding `timeoutSeconds`. The generic host cannot know why a given tool stalls, so domain-specific advice belongs to the extension. Omit to print the neutral message alone.

environmentOption.description: A generic per-invocation environment-selector flag: the host adds this as a shared Commander option on every command the extension contributes and forwards the parsed value to the upstream process as the named env var. The host has no knowledge of what the flag or env var MEAN — it just wires option → env var — so a new extension can add its own per-invocation selector with zero host change.

boundary.description: Interpolated directory that the resolved write path must stay within (path-traversal guard). Defaults to the process working directory. Commands that target a project via an option such as --path MUST set this to the same resolved root as `path` (e.g. `${path | absoluteOrCwd}`), otherwise a valid --path write is refused as "outside project directory".
